subject: lavaan warns that a solution has NOT been found

messages.author: c15d2c2a9d84d268
messages.subject: lavaan warns that a solution has NOT been found
parts: I encountered this warning when performing a CFA on a scale with 12 items. My initial idea was that one of the items was either containing coding errors or too little variance. However, check of the data did not suggest any of these problems. Then I tried to identify a "bad" item by removing each item one-by-one. It turned out that removing any of 10 items resulted in convergence of the model (with very good fits). So, any of 10 different compositions of 11 items yielded convergence. Can anyone tell me why analyzing all 12 items result in non-convergence?

Some information is needed to identify the problem.
The problem may reside in a small sample size, low correlation between items, or both.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: lavaan warns that a solution has NOT been found
parts:
Can you also post the full error message, and any other warnings it produced?  

Your sample size is quite small relative to the amount of data.  N = 159 yields only about 2 observations for each of 12*13/2 = 78 unique elements in the covariance matrix.  So it might be an empirical underidentification issue.

But the fact that the model converges on any of 10 (why not 12? Could you not remove 2 of them?) combinations of 11 items makes this seem more like a possible redundancy issue.  Try det(ang) to see if the determinant is positive.  If it is zero or negative, then the matrix is nonpositive definite, indicating probable linear dependencies among the variables.  Even though the largest correlation is only 0.64, there might be multicollinearity hiding somewhere (e.g., if you have all scale items AND the scale total in a correlation matrix).

The full error message reads:

Warning message:
In lavaan::lavaan(model = model.ang, data = ang, ordered = angitems,  :
  lavaan WARNING: the optimizer warns that a solution has NOT been found!

Removing any of 10 items resulted in convergence of the model. Indeed, removing any of 2 items (of the 12 items) did NOT solve the problem.
The determinant of the matrix is:

> det(cor(ang))
[1] 0.007854231
